planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from drying wind.

directions: Onychium japonicum, the carrot fern, is an East Asian woodland fern prized for finely dissected, blue-green to gray-green fronds that resemble carrot-top foliage rather than typical fern pinnae, giving it a soft, feathery texture distinct from most shade ferns. It spreads by slender creeping rhizomes to form a loose, low colony rather than a solitary clump, making it useful as a textural groundcover threading between hostas, hellebores, and other woodland perennials. Fronds are semi-evergreen and may collapse in harder winters, but the hardy rhizomes resprout reliably from below ground each spring. Provide humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade for the best frond quality.

planting.note: Plant rhizome sections in a shallow, fast-draining, humus-rich mix in spring, keeping the fuzzy rhizomes exposed on the surface rather than buried.

directions: Davallia mariesii is a deciduous East Asian fern whose thick, silvery-brown, fur-covered rhizomes creep visibly across the soil surface or over the rim of a container, giving rise to the common name squirrel's foot fern. It is markedly more cold-hardy than the tropical Davallia trichomanoides and Davallia fejeensis already familiar in cultivation, dying back to the rhizome in winter but resprouting reliably each spring in a climate with a real chill. Grow it in a shallow, fast-draining, humus-rich mix in a hanging basket, on a mounted slab, or as a groundcover over rock in partial to full shade. Established plants tolerate brief dry spells better than most woodland ferns thanks to their thick, moisture-storing rhizomes.

planting.note: Plant divisions or rooted leaf plantlets in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Taff's Gold is a variegated sport of the Pacific Northwest native piggyback plant, its rounded, hairy, maple-shaped leaves irregularly speckled and splashed with cream to pale yellow over green, brightening shaded plantings that would otherwise rely on plain green foliage. Like the species, it reproduces by small plantlets that form at the base of each mature leaf and root wherever the leaf touches moist soil, so a single division quickly increases into a colony. Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade, since the shallow roots and thin leaves wilt quickly if the soil dries out. The cream variegation is generally most pronounced with a bit more light than full deep shade, though direct sun will scorch the pale leaf tissue.

common_name: Variegated Tongue Fern (Cream-Splashed Japanese Felt Fern)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in a fast-draining, humus-rich mix over rock or in shallow soil in partial to full shade.

directions: 'Variegata' is a cream-and-green variegated form of the Japanese felt fern, its thick, undivided, tongue-shaped fronds irregularly streaked and marbled with creamy white rather than solid green, giving it a brighter presence than the species on rock walls, tree bases, or shaded slopes. Like the straight species, it develops a felted coat of rusty-brown scales on the frond undersides and tolerates far more drought than typical finely cut ferns once established. Grow it in a fast-draining, humus-rich mix over rock, bark, or shallow soil in partial to full shade, letting the surface dry slightly between waterings. Variegation is generally best expressed with a bit more filtered light than the deep shade the species itself will tolerate, though harsh direct sun will scorch the pale leaf tissue.
